specification.title: An inner transaction that promises independence commits; then the outer transaction rolls back
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of two connections.
Write the marker `outer` through the framework's ordinary write API. The framework decides when it is sent: one with a unit of work may keep it pending.
Start an inner transaction through the framework's API that promises an independent transaction (for example a REQUIRES_NEW propagation). Write the marker `inner` in it.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the inner transaction's pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid().
End the inner transaction normally, so that it commits.
Raise an application error in the outer scope, so that the framework rolls the outer transaction back.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: An inner transaction started through an API that promises an independent transaction commits only its own writes: the outer scope's writes, whether already sent or still pending in the framework, are committed only by the outer transaction.

execution.description: DB.Transaction. The callback catches the unique violation and returns nil, so GORM calls Commit. A nested DB.Transaction is a savepoint. sql.TxOptions.Isolation is passed to DB.Transaction for TX-05. SkipDefaultTransaction and DisableNestedTransaction keep their defaults.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The caller knows that the inner transaction committed and the outer one rolled back. From the API alone, it cannot see which transaction carried a write the framework still had pending.

evaluation.reason: GORM has no propagation mode that commits an inner transaction while an outer transaction stays open. A nested DB.Transaction or SavePoint is a SAVEPOINT on the same connection. DisableNestedTransaction false is the default and still uses a savepoint. This adapter does not open a second *sql.DB and call it an independent transaction.

reproduction.requires: pnpm run setup, then pnpm run pg:up (README.md)
